Exact Paired Sign-Flip Tests of Within-Subject Differences

Source: R/analysis-paired.R
ExactPairedTests.Rd

For each declared group of rows, tests whether paired differences are symmetric about zero with the exact Wilcoxon signed-rank test over all \(2^n\) sign assignments, together with the exact two-sided sign test and, optionally, a Clopper-Pearson interval for the fraction of subjects whose difference lies in an expected direction. Leave-one-subject-out results can be requested instead of the full tests.

Usage

ExactPairedTests(
  data,
  value,
  groups = NULL,
  id = NULL,
  expected = NULL,
  family = NULL,
  omit = c("none", "each"),
  conf_level = 0.95,
  max_n = 500L
)

Arguments

data

Data frame in long form: one row per subject and test.

value

Name of the numeric difference column (for a one-sample test, the values themselves).

groups

Optional names of columns that define separate tests. NULL treats all rows as one test. Output groups follow first appearance.

id

Optional subject column; required for omit = "each". Subjects must be unique within a group.

expected

Optional expected direction: "less" or "greater" for every group, or the name of a column holding "less"/"greater" (constant within a group). Adds the number of subjects in that direction and its Clopper-Pearson interval.

family

Optional columns defining multiplicity families; adds family_id (values joined by " :: "). hypothesis_id joins the group values the same way. Both are ready for AdjustPatientFamilies().

omit

"none" (full tests) or "each": one row per group and omitted subject (all subjects of the group, in data order), with the omitted subject in column omitted.

conf_level

Confidence level of the direction interval.

max_n

Largest number of nonzero differences accepted.

Value

A data frame with the group columns, n_available, n_nonzero, n_zero, positive, negative, median_difference and mean_difference (of the nonzero differences), signed_rank_sum, p_value (signed-rank), sign_p_value, status, optionally expected, expected_direction, direction_ci_low, direction_ci_high, conf_level, and hypothesis_id (plus family_id).

Details

Non-finite differences are unavailable; zero differences are excluded from the signed-rank and sign tests (they still count as available subjects and as not being in the expected direction). Ranks of absolute differences use midranks for ties. The two-sided p value is the fraction of sign assignments whose absolute signed-rank sum is at least the observed one. It is computed by dynamic programming over twice the midranks (integers), so it equals full enumeration exactly for up to 52 nonzero differences without enumerating them.

See also

PairedDifferences(), AdjustPatientFamilies()

Examples

d <- data.frame(test = rep(c("a", "b"), each = 6), subject = rep(1:6, 2),
                difference = c(-3, -1, -2, -5, 1, -4, 2, -1, 3, 0, 1, 2))
ExactPairedTests(d, "difference", groups = "test", id = "subject",
                 expected = "less")
#>   test n_available n_nonzero n_zero positive negative median_difference
#> 1    a           6         6      0        1        5              -2.5
#> 2    b           6         5      1        4        1               2.0
#>   mean_difference signed_rank_sum p_value sign_p_value status expected
#> 1       -2.333333             -18 0.09375      0.21875  EXACT     less
#> 2        1.400000              12 0.18750      0.37500  EXACT     less
#>   expected_direction direction_ci_low direction_ci_high conf_level
#> 1                  5      0.358765421         0.9957893       0.95
#> 2                  1      0.004210745         0.6412346       0.95
#>   hypothesis_id
#> 1             a
#> 2             b
ExactPairedTests(d, "difference", groups = "test", id = "subject",
                 omit = "each")
#>    test omitted n_available n_nonzero n_zero positive negative
#> 1     a       1           5         5      0        1        4
#> 2     a       2           5         5      0        1        4
#> 3     a       3           5         5      0        1        4
#> 4     a       4           5         5      0        1        4
#> 5     a       5           5         5      0        0        5
#> 6     a       6           5         5      0        1        4
#> 7     b       1           5         4      1        3        1
#> 8     b       2           5         4      1        4        0
#> 9     b       3           5         4      1        3        1
#> 10    b       4           5         5      0        4        1
#> 11    b       5           5         4      1        3        1
#> 12    b       6           5         4      1        3        1
#>    median_difference mean_difference signed_rank_sum p_value sign_p_value
#> 1               -2.0           -2.20             -12  0.1875       0.3750
#> 2               -3.0           -2.60             -13  0.1250       0.3750
#> 3               -3.0           -2.40             -12  0.1875       0.3750
#> 4               -2.0           -1.80             -12  0.1875       0.3750
#> 5               -3.0           -3.00             -15  0.0625       0.0625
#> 6               -2.0           -2.00             -12  0.1875       0.3750
#> 7                1.5            1.25               7  0.3750       0.6250
#> 8                2.0            2.00              10  0.1250       0.1250
